purpose: Landmark-compatible constraint system for selecting the canonical shoulder girdle without fitting back to the r95 mesh.

lateral_acromion_to_AC_joint_mm.definition: straight distance from lateral acromion to AC joint

clavicle_endpoint_length_mm.definition: straight 3D distance between lateral-most clavicular point in AC joint and medial-most clavicular point in SC joint

AC_breadth_from_mean_outer_breadth_and_m.derivation: If d is the 3D lateral-acromion→AC distance, its transverse component t satisfies 0<t<=d. Therefore biAC = biacromial - 2t and biacromial-2d <= biAC < biacromial.
AC_breadth_from_mean_outer_breadth_and_m.warning: The earlier version incorrectly treated the 3D distance as a purely transverse offset. That equality has been withdrawn.

AC_breadth_conservative_1sd_bounds_mm.derivation: lower = biacromial_1sd_low - 2*(AC-distance_1sd_high); upper remains below biacromial_1sd_high

derived_constraints.current_a003_still_invalid_reason: a003 bi-AC breadth exceeds even the outer biacromial breadth; this conclusion does not depend on decomposing the 3D acromion→AC distance.

hard_geometry_rules: each_SC_to_AC_3D_chord should lie in an endpoint-length adult-male corridor after stature/sex context is reconciled
AC and GH remain distinct centres
lateral acromion remains lateral to AC joint
left/right canonical geometry is mirrored except where an explicit asymmetry policy is applied
acceptance_logic: Reject any candidate whose bi-AC breadth equals or exceeds its bilateral lateral-acromion (biacromial) breadth.

Treat the measured lateral-acromion→AC distance as a 3D distance. Its transverse component may be smaller; never subtract the full 3D distance from biacromial breadth as an equality unless source geometry proves the vector is purely transverse.
Reject any candidate whose required transverse acromion→AC offset exceeds the selected 3D acromion→AC distance.
Reject any candidate whose SC-to-AC straight chord exceeds the clavicle curved centreline length.
Do not force the scapular GH-to-inferior-angle span to a value until the 3D scapular landmark frame is solved.
Do not move the whole shoulder vertically just to repair width: acromial height is already close to the stature-conditioned scaffold.
interpretation: The old a003 shoulder width remains directly invalid: its bilateral AC breadth (~481 mm) is larger than the expected OUTER biacromial breadth (~425 mm), although AC joints must lie medial to the lateral acromial points.
The cadaveric 34±8 mm lateral-acromion→AC measurement is a 3D distance, so it constrains—not directly determines—the transverse AC offset.
Exact bilateral AC breadth must come from the combined clavicle orientation/endpoint solution plus the outer acromial scaffold.
next_steps: Solve SC/AC/acromion coordinates in 3D against the clavicle endpoint/centreline constraints and global shoulder-height scaffold.
Build the scapular local landmark frame independently, then place GH from the retained local depth and glenoid geometry.
Rerun shoulder-complex solver tests after the canonical girdle coordinates are instantiated.

audit_correction_2026_10_08.issue: Earlier derivation subtracted a 3D acromion→AC distance as if it were purely transverse.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.correction: Use it only as an upper bound on the transverse medial offset. The a003 excessive-width conclusion is unchanged because bi-AC already exceeds outer biacromial breadth.
